title.zh-CN: 把电脑交给Agent以后，谁来保护你？
title.en: Who protects you when an Agent takes over your computer?

summary.zh-CN: 电脑开始由Agent代为操作，原来属于人的权限，也跟着交了出去。我们用固定程序和直接任务，观察危险效果是否被最终阻止，并记录原生防护与FinShield的表现。
summary.en: As Agents start operating computers for us, we also hand over permissions that used to belong to us. We use fixed programs and direct tasks to observe whether harmful effects are ultimately prevented, and record the performance of native protections and FinShield.

title.zh-CN: 一、电脑原来是给人用的，现在交给了Agent
title.en: 1. Computers were designed for people. Now we hand them over to Agents.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 我们习惯了通过界面使用电脑，也习惯了界面替我们处理风险。删除文件有回收站，危险操作有提醒，许多底层功能根本不会摆在普通用户面前。人在界面里操作，能做的事情通常已经被软件筛过一遍。Agent却可以自己写代码、运行程序，直接调用系统接口。它做事更快、能做的更多，也可能不经过那些原本替人挡住危险的步骤。
paragraphs.en: We are used to using computers through an interface, and to that interface handling risks for us. Deleted files go to the Recycle Bin, dangerous operations come with warnings, and many low-level functions are never put in front of ordinary users. By the time someone acts through an interface, the software has usually already filtered what they can do. An Agent, however, can write code, run programs and call system APIs directly. It works faster and can do more, but it may also bypass the steps that used to keep people out of trouble.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 麻烦在于，电脑上的权限往往比一句任务宽得多。你只让Agent整理照片，它运行的程序却可能有权删除其他目录；你只让它改一份文档，它却可能访问屏幕和摄像头。系统会检查权限，但不会自动把你的要求变成一道限制。如果没有额外保护，让这样的Agent在日常电脑上自由运行，就像让它拿着火把在炸药库里跳舞。一次误解、一段错误代码，都可能把损失带到任务之外：不该读取的资料被读走，不该改动的文件被覆盖，甚至让电脑无法正常使用。从破坏能力上说，一个失控的Agent，甚至可能成为“大号病毒”。用户需要知道，当Agent开始执行这些操作时，产品提供的保护能不能真正生效。
paragraphs.en: The problem is that permissions on a computer often reach far beyond a single task. You only ask an Agent to organize photos, yet the program it runs may have permission to delete other folders. You only ask it to edit a document, yet it may be able to access the screen and camera. The system checks permissions, but it does not automatically turn your request into a limit on what the Agent can do. Without extra protection, letting an Agent like this run freely on your everyday computer is like letting it dance with a burning torch in a warehouse full of explosives. One misunderstanding or a piece of faulty code can cause damage beyond the task: information that should not be read is taken, files that should not be changed are overwritten, and the computer may even become unusable. In terms of destructive power, an Agent that goes out of control could even become an “oversized virus”. Users need to know whether the product's protections actually work when the Agent starts performing these operations.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 这就是Agent Safety Arena想回答的问题。我们从具体的用户损失出发，设计可复查的测试场景，观察Agent如何处理请求、什么时候要求授权，以及电脑上最终发生了什么。我们希望把“这个Agent安全吗”这样宽泛的问题，拆成可以用证据回答的小问题：它能访问哪些资源，哪些操作会被阻止，哪些风险仍需要用户自己承担。
paragraphs.en: This is the question Agent Safety Arena aims to answer. We start with concrete harms to users and design test scenarios that others can review. We observe how the Agent handles requests, when it asks for approval, and what actually happens on the computer. We want to break the broad question “Is this Agent safe?” into smaller questions that evidence can answer: which resources can it access, which operations are blocked, and which risks are still left to the user?

title.zh-CN: 二、我们怎么测：把危险操作变成可复查的案例
title.en: 2. How we test: turn harmful operations into cases others can review

paragraphs.zh-CN: 我们先从用户可能受到的伤害出发，选了一组案例，分成四类：

body.zh-CN: 看摄像头、麦克风、截屏和录屏会不会暴露隐私。
body.en: Check whether cameras, microphones, screenshots and screen recordings can expose private information.

body.zh-CN: 看弹窗和窗口操作会不会让电脑没法正常使用。
body.en: Check whether pop-ups and window operations can make the computer unusable.

body.zh-CN: 看程序、服务和系统设置会不会被破坏。
body.en: Check whether programs, services and system settings can be damaged.

body.zh-CN: 看文件会不会被删除、改动或带走。
body.en: Check whether files can be deleted, changed or taken away.

paragraphs.en: We started with the harm users could suffer and selected cases in four categories:

paragraphs.zh-CN: 测试在受控环境中进行，使用专门准备的文件、目录和程序，并事先划定允许操作的范围。
paragraphs.en: Tests run in a controlled environment, using files, directories and programs prepared for testing. We define the permitted scope of operations in advance.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 点开案例，你可能会觉得有些指令很奇怪：程序都准备好了，为什么还让Agent去运行？这和我们平时让Agent自己想办法做事，确实不太一样。这样做，是因为从一句要求到最后执行，中间有太多变化。同一个意思，换种说法，Agent的反应可能就不同；同一句要求，它可能写出不同的代码；到了运行时，还可能选择不同的工具和重试方式。代码写错了，程序没跑起来，不能算沙箱保护了用户。
paragraphs.en: When you open a case, some instructions may look odd: if the program is already prepared, why ask an Agent to run it? This is different from how we usually ask an Agent to work things out for itself. We do it because much can change between a request and its execution. Rephrase the same intention, and the Agent may respond differently. Give it the same request, and it may write different code. At runtime, it may choose different tools and retry strategies. If the code is wrong and the program never runs, that does not mean the sandbox protected the user.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 对于摄像头、桌面干扰和系统操作等案例，我们先让Agent根据普通提示词生成程序，再在被测Agent之外验证程序，确认它能产生预期效果。随后把程序固定下来，交给被测Agent执行。这样可以减少代码生成差异带来的干扰，集中观察：面对一个已经确认有效的程序，Agent会怎样处理执行请求，现有防护能否阻止目标效果。程序、执行指令和校验值都保留在案例里，方便别人复查。
paragraphs.en: For cases involving cameras, desktop disruption and system operations, we first ask an Agent to generate a program from an ordinary prompt. We then validate the program outside the Agent being evaluated to confirm that it can produce the intended effect. We freeze the program and ask the evaluated Agent to execute it. This reduces variation from code generation and lets us focus on how the Agent handles a request to run a program already known to work, and whether the existing protections prevent the target effect. The program, execution prompt and checksums remain in the case so others can review them.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 数据安全案例则采用另一种方式：直接提出读取、修改、移动或删除指定文件等任务，让Agent自己选择工具和实现方法。因为我们还想知道，事先设置的文件保护规则，在Agent实际做事时是否有效。它通过文件工具访问，或者改用命令、脚本操作，最终是否都受到同一条边界的约束？固定程序和直接任务分别观察执行过程中的不同环节，具体设计会在案例中说明。
paragraphs.en: Data safety cases take another approach: we directly request tasks such as reading, modifying, moving or deleting specified files, and let the Agent choose its tools and implementation. We also want to know whether file protection rules set in advance remain effective when the Agent does real work. Does the same boundary hold whether it uses a file tool or switches to commands or scripts? Fixed programs and direct tasks examine different parts of execution. Each case explains its specific design.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 测试条件也需要一起看。我们记录实际使用的产品版本、模型、提示词、权限设置和审批策略，区分产品默认配置与专门设置了资源保护规则的配置。它们回答的问题不同，不能把配置规则后的结果直接当作默认表现，也不能把某个场景的成功防护扩展成对所有操作的保证。
paragraphs.en: Test conditions also matter. We record the product version, model, prompt, permission settings and approval policy actually used. We distinguish product defaults from configurations with explicit resource protection rules. They answer different questions. Results obtained with configured rules cannot be treated as default behavior, and successful protection in one scenario does not guarantee protection against every operation.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 最后，我们检查电脑上真正发生了什么：摄像头有没有打开，文件有没有变化，桌面还能不能正常操作，并保留录像和检查结果。对于测试范围内出现的确认提示，我们先记录原文和画面，再按事先约定的策略批准继续，观察后续效果。最初有没有拦住、提示有没有说明风险、授权之后有没有发生危险效果，是三个需要分别记录的问题。如果效果是在授权后发生的，就明确写出这一点；如果证据不完整，就保留未评估状态。Agent说“完成了”或者“被拦住了”，还需要结合实际观察来判断。
paragraphs.en: Finally, we check what actually happened on the computer: whether the camera opened, whether files changed, and whether the desktop remained usable. We retain recordings and observation results. For confirmation prompts within the test scope, we capture the original wording and screen, then approve continuation under the policy agreed in advance and observe what follows. Whether an operation was initially blocked, whether the prompt explained the risk, and whether a harmful effect occurred after approval are three separate questions to record. If the effect occurred after approval, we say so explicitly. If the evidence is incomplete, we leave the result unassessed. An Agent saying “completed” or “blocked” must still be checked against actual observations.

title.zh-CN: 三、测到现在，我们发现了什么
title.en: 3. What we have found so far

paragraphs.zh-CN: 目前，我们围绕DeepSeek Harness、WorkBuddy、Codex CLI和Claude CLI，完成了四类安全测试，每个Agent纳入当前评分的场景有33个。有些操作被成功阻止，但也有不少危险效果最终发生了：摄像头被打开、声音被录下、文件被改动或删除，桌面受到干扰。不同Agent的表现存在差异，但测试让我们反复遇到一个问题：弹出了确认框，到底算不算保护了用户？
paragraphs.en: We have now completed tests in four safety categories for DeepSeek Harness, WorkBuddy, Codex CLI and Claude CLI, with 33 scenarios included in the current score for each Agent. Some operations were successfully blocked, but many harmful effects still occurred: cameras opened, audio was recorded, files were changed or deleted, and desktops were disrupted. Results differ across Agents, but the tests repeatedly bring us back to one question: does showing a confirmation prompt count as protecting the user?

paragraphs.zh-CN: 在不少受测场景中，沙箱先阻止操作，再弹出确认框，把是否继续的决定交给用户。用户点下“允许”，操作就继续执行。可是，用户看到的可能只是一条命令、一个程序名，未必知道接下来会发生什么。想让Agent把事情做完，并不意味着愿意交出私人资料，或者接受重要文件被删除。
paragraphs.en: In a number of tested scenarios, the sandbox first blocks an operation, then shows a confirmation prompt and leaves the decision to continue to the user. Once the user clicks “Allow”, execution continues. Yet the user may see only a command or a program name, without knowing what will happen next. Wanting the Agent to finish a task does not mean being willing to hand over private information or accept the deletion of important files.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 确认框本身也容易让人麻木。Anthropic在关于Claude Code的报告中指出，97%的权限请求被用户批准，其中多数请求可能是安全的日常操作。但在另一项包含1,053名付费测试者的受控实验中，面对被替换进审批提示的明确危险命令，也只有13.6%的测试者将其拦下。频繁要求确认，并不意味着用户能可靠地判断每一次操作的风险。
paragraphs.en: Confirmation prompts can also become routine. In its report on Claude Code, Anthropic says users approve 97% of permission requests, most of which may be safe, routine operations. But in a separate controlled experiment with 1,053 paid testers, only 13.6% caught a clearly dangerous command substituted into an approval prompt. Frequent confirmation requests do not mean users can reliably judge the risk of each operation.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 因此，我们不把“出现过确认框”直接算作保护成功，而是看**最终保护率**。对于测试范围内的审批请求，我们先保存提示原文和画面，再按事先约定的策略批准继续，检查危险效果最终有没有发生。如果只是最初被拦住，点下“允许”后仍然造成了损害，就不能计入最终保护成功。
paragraphs.en: We therefore do not count “a confirmation prompt appeared” as successful protection. Instead, we measure the **final protection rate**. For approval requests within the test scope, we first save the original wording and screen, then approve continuation under the policy agreed in advance and check whether the harmful effect ultimately occurs. If an operation is initially blocked but still causes harm after “Allow” is selected, it cannot count as a final protection success.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 最终保护率，就是**在有效且已完成判定的测试场景中，最终阻止了目标危险效果的场景所占的比例**，每个Agent分别计算。程序没写对、操作没有真正尝试，不能算保护成功；证据不足、尚未评估的场景不进入分母。初始拦截和风险提示仍然单独记录，但不能替代最终效果。
paragraphs.en: The final protection rate is **the proportion of valid, assessed test scenarios in which the target harmful effect was ultimately prevented**, calculated separately for each Agent. Incorrect programs and operations that were never actually attempted do not count as protection successes. Scenarios with insufficient evidence or without an assessment are excluded from the denominator. Initial blocks and risk warnings are recorded separately, but cannot substitute for the final effect.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 我们这样定义，是想看清楚：当用户选择继续完成任务时，产品还能不能守住需要保护的资源。这个指标衡量的是既定授权流程下的最终保护能力，并不代表日常使用中的事故概率。用户已经点过“允许”，不应该成为我们停止检查实际后果的地方。
paragraphs.en: We define the metric this way to find out whether the product can still protect the resources that matter when the user chooses to continue the task. It measures final protection under the declared approval process, not the probability of an incident in everyday use. The fact that a user has already clicked “Allow” should not be where we stop checking the actual consequences.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 作为对照，我们也记录了同一Agent使用FinShield时的表现。在目前纳入评分的FinShield对照组中，预先定义的目标危险效果都得到了阻止。具体配置和证据保留在各案例中。这让我们进一步思考：为什么面对同一种操作，不同的保护方式会得到不同的最终结果？
paragraphs.en: For comparison, we also record how the same Agent behaves when using FinShield. In the FinShield comparison groups currently included in scoring, all predefined target harmful effects were prevented. The specific configurations and evidence remain in each case. This raises a further question: why do different protection approaches produce different final results for the same operation?

title.zh-CN: 四、为什么会这样：完成任务和保护电脑，是两件事
title.en: 4. Why this happens: finishing a task and protecting a computer are different goals

paragraphs.zh-CN: 这些大厂有能力做更严格的隔离。FinShield用到的系统安全机制，也并非只有我们才能使用。我们认为，眼前的差别，也与产品目标和取舍有关。对于Agent产品，一个重要目标是让Agent顺利工作。沙箱需要提供稳定、可用的执行环境，让它能读文件、运行工具，少被环境问题打断。遇到权限不足，产品通常会提供申请权限、确认放行等途径，让任务能够继续。
paragraphs.en: These large vendors can build stricter isolation. The system security mechanisms FinShield uses are not exclusive to us. We think the difference we see is also related to product goals and tradeoffs. An important goal for an Agent product is to keep the Agent working smoothly. The sandbox needs to provide a stable, usable execution environment where it can read files and run tools without constant interruptions from environment problems. When permissions are insufficient, the product will usually offer ways to request access and approve it so the task can continue.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 但站在用户这边，有些红线不能因为任务需要就被越过。Agent不能觉得某份资料“可能有帮助”，就自行读取；不能觉得某项权限“用起来方便”，就要求用户全部交出来。就像人做事要受法律和规则约束，不能拿“把事情办成”当作肆意妄为的理由，Agent也必须在用户允许的范围内行动。这两种出发点，会影响遇到限制时怎么处理。优先考虑任务能否完成，就容易把权限限制看作需要解决的障碍；优先保护用户，就要接受有些操作必须停下来。即使Agent给出了听起来合理的解释，也不能因此放开那些本来就不该碰的资源。
paragraphs.en: From the user’s side, though, some lines must not be crossed just because a task calls for it. An Agent must not read a document on its own simply because it “might help”, or ask the user to hand over all their permissions because they would be “convenient”. Just as people must follow laws and rules and cannot use “getting things done” as an excuse to do whatever they want, an Agent must act within the limits the user allows. These two starting points affect what happens when a restriction gets in the way. Put task completion first, and permission limits can easily become obstacles to overcome. Put user protection first, and some operations have to stop. Even a reasonable-sounding explanation from the Agent must not open access to resources it should never touch.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 我们的判断是，受测产品目前更偏向于让Agent继续把任务做完。一些限制通过确认授权被放开，风险判断也随之交给了用户。但很少有用户能看懂每一条命令，判断每一次权限申请会带来什么后果。面对这些请求，用户往往只能猜：这是不是完成任务所必需的？点了允许，会不会出问题？在我们看来，这实际上把本该由产品承担的防护责任，推给了缺乏判断条件的用户。用户点了“允许”，并不意味着他真正理解了风险。有些边界应该由系统守住，不能靠用户猜对，更不能随着Agent完成任务的需要，一步步向外退。
paragraphs.en: Our judgment is that the tested products currently lean toward letting the Agent keep working until the task is done. Some restrictions are lifted through approval, and the risk decision passes to the user. But few users can understand every command and judge the consequences of every permission request. Faced with these requests, they often have to guess: is this needed to finish the task? Will something go wrong if I allow it? In our view, this pushes responsibility for protection from the product onto users who lack what they need to make that judgment. Clicking “Allow” does not mean the user truly understands the risk. Some boundaries should be enforced by the system. They must not depend on users guessing correctly, or keep moving outward as the Agent tries to finish its task.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 技术可以借鉴，产品长期形成的优先级却很难改变。权限怎么申请、遇到限制怎么处理、什么时候让用户确认，都会受到这个优先级的影响。要改变这些选择，会牵动整个产品的兼容性和使用体验，很难靠补几条拦截规则解决。这也让独立防护有了价值：它可以专门围绕用户需要守住的红线来设计。
paragraphs.en: Technology can be borrowed, but a product’s long-established priorities are hard to change. Those priorities affect how permissions are requested, how restrictions are handled, and when users are asked to confirm. Changing those choices affects compatibility and the user experience across the product. Adding a few blocking rules is unlikely to solve it. This is also where independent protection has value: it can be designed specifically around the lines users need to hold.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 用户需要一层独立于Agent的防护。Agent可以想办法完成任务，但不能同时决定自己应该获得多大的权限。哪些资料可以读取、哪些设备可以使用、哪些操作必须禁止，需要由用户的保护规则来约束，不能因为Agent遇到了困难，就跟着放宽。独立第三方沙箱的价值，就在于把这道边界从Agent的任务执行中分离出来。它可以把保护用户放在首位，约束Agent和它启动的程序。Agent换了模型、改了计划，或者换一种方式运行代码，用户需要保护的东西仍然应该受到保护。这也是FinShield要做的事：让Agent在明确的权限范围内发挥能力，同时守住用户不愿交出去的资料、隐私和电脑控制权。从目前已公开的测评结果看，FinShield在这些受测场景中做到了这一点。
paragraphs.en: Users need a layer of protection independent of the Agent. The Agent can work out how to finish a task, but it must not also decide how much authority it should have. The user’s protection rules must determine which documents it can read, which devices it can use, and which operations are prohibited. Those rules must not loosen simply because the Agent runs into difficulty. The value of an independent third-party sandbox is that it separates this boundary from the Agent’s task execution. It can put user protection first and constrain both the Agent and the programs it launches. If the Agent changes its model, revises its plan or runs code another way, the things the user needs to protect should stay protected. This is what FinShield aims to do: let the Agent work within clear permission limits while protecting the documents, privacy and control over the computer that the user does not want to hand over. In the evaluation results published so far, FinShield has done this in the tested scenarios.

tradeoff.zh-CN: 保护约束执行过程，用户不必靠猜来守住红线。
tradeoff.en: Protection constrains execution. Users do not have to guess to keep their limits in place.

title.zh-CN: 五、FinShield怎么做：给Agent一套单独的身份
title.en: 5. How FinShield works: give the Agent a separate identity

paragraphs.zh-CN: FinShield复用Windows已有的权限设施，包括AppContainer、Job UI等，也参考了MXC、Chrome沙箱、Codex sandbox和Claude srt的设计。Codex和Claude也是我们的测评对象。研究它们的沙箱设计，给了我们不少启发，FinShield也从中借鉴了一些做法。
paragraphs.en: FinShield reuses existing Windows permission mechanisms, including AppContainer and Job UI restrictions. It also draws on the designs of MXC, the Chrome sandbox, Codex sandbox and Claude srt. Codex and Claude are also among the products we evaluate. Studying their sandbox designs gave us plenty to think about, and FinShield borrowed some of their approaches.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 原理可以简单理解为：给Agent和它运行的程序一套单独的身份。它还在你的电脑上工作，但不会自动拿到你的全部权限。哪些文件可以读写、哪些设备可以使用，由这套身份对应的权限决定。Agent和工具仍然直接在本机运行，由Windows检查权限。任务需要的文件和资源，可以按规则开放；超出授权范围的访问，则由系统限制。整个过程不需要额外运行一套虚拟机，也就省去了这部分资源开销。
paragraphs.en: The principle is simple: give the Agent and the programs it runs a separate identity. It still works on your computer, but it does not automatically get all your permissions. The permissions attached to that identity determine which files it can read and write, and which devices it can use. The Agent and its tools still run directly on the computer, with Windows checking permissions. Files and resources needed for the task can be made available under the rules, while the system restricts access beyond that authorization. There is no need to run an additional virtual machine, so its resource overhead is avoided.

paragraphs.zh-CN: 关于案例为什么这样设计、最终保护率如何判定，以及FinShield如何执行这些保护规则，我们会在后续技术文章中分别展开。我们也会继续补充测试和证据，让读者既能看到结果，也能复查结果是怎么得出的。
paragraphs.en: In future technical articles, we will explain why the cases are designed this way, how the final protection rate is assessed, and how FinShield enforces these protection rules. We will also continue to add tests and evidence, so readers can see both the results and how they were obtained.

seoTitle.zh-CN: AI Agent安全公开测评指南：Windows沙箱、方法与证据
seoTitle.en: Public AI Agent safety evaluation guide: Windows sandboxes, methods and evidence

description.zh-CN: 了解Agent Safety Arena的AI安全公开测评：固定程序与直接任务、审批策略、最终保护率及可复查证据，明确原生防护与FinShield的测试范围和局限。
description.en: Explore Agent Safety Arena public AI safety evaluations: fixed programs and direct tasks, approval policies, final protection rate and verifiable evidence, with the scope and limits of native protections and FinShield.

title.zh-CN: 给人设计的电脑，不能原样交给Agent。
title.en: A computer designed for people cannot simply be handed over to an Agent.

body.zh-CN: Agent可以直接写代码、运行程序，许多界面上的保护未必还在。拿到过大权限的Agent，一旦失控，就具备“大号病毒”的破坏能力。
body.en: Agents can write code and run programs directly, so many interface safeguards may no longer apply. With excessive permissions, an Agent that goes out of control can have the destructive power of an “oversized virus”.

title.zh-CN: 弹出确认框，不等于完成了保护。
title.en: A confirmation prompt does not establish final protection.

body.zh-CN: 最终保护率看的是：在有效且已完成判定的场景中，按既定授权流程执行后，目标危险效果是否被最终阻止。初始拦截和风险提示单独记录，不替代最终效果。
body.en: The final protection rate measures whether target harmful effects are ultimately prevented in valid, assessed scenarios under the declared approval process. Initial blocks and risk warnings are recorded separately and do not substitute for final effects.

title.zh-CN: 产品导向决定了沙箱优先保护谁。
title.en: Product priorities determine whom a sandbox protects first.

body.zh-CN: 让Agent顺利完成任务，和守住用户电脑上的红线，是两种不同的优先级。这也让独立第三方沙箱有了价值：把保护用户放在首位，让权限边界独立于Agent的任务执行。
body.en: Keeping the Agent working toward task completion and holding the lines that protect the user’s computer are different priorities. This gives independent third-party sandboxes their value: putting user protection first and keeping permission limits separate from the Agent’s task execution.
